spec: dispatch://LEGION-163/spec version 2 (Summary, Acceptance 1-4, Design, Rejected). Architect ruling carried into this plan: the constructor THROWS; no type-level refusal; the Kubernetes runtime still constructs without `run`.
summary: The daemon entry point (`packages/daemon/src/daemon/index.ts`, `startDaemonLocked`) builds `ProcessManager` without `run: runner` since #1031 (`d30f820c`); under the tmux runtime (`TmuxRuntime.removesWorkspacesOnTreeClose = true`) every tree close reaches `ProcessManager.workspaceCommandRunner` (processes.ts ~3129) with `deps.run` undefined and logs `failed to remove the workspace of ... : runtime owns workspace cleanup but ProcessManager has no command runner`. Four changes: (1) pass `run: runner` again; (2) the `ProcessManager` constructor throws when `deps.runtime.removesWorkspacesOnTreeClose` is true and `deps.run` is undefined, naming the runtime (`deps.config.runtime.name`) and the missing runner; (3) a `startDaemon`-level test in index.test.ts that is RED on `af232beb` (today's main) and GREEN after, plus a constructor-refusal test in processes.test.ts with a companion assertion that a retaining runtime constructs without `run`; (4) one sentence in `packages/daemon/src/daemon/AGENTS.md`.
nonGoals: No sweep of workspaces left by trees closed while the wiring was broken (LEGION-104 rejected a second owner of the workspace directories).
No retry of a failed removal (LEGION-104: logged once, never retried).
No type-level Runtime discrimination (`Runtime` stays one interface; `ProcessManagerDeps.run` stays optional).

No smoke rig or scratch daemon for this issue; the production-like proof is the daemon's own boot path under the test harness (a surface the legion-worker skill names), and acceptance 3 is the live daemon's next tree close after the operator's restart.

tasks.why: Spec acceptance 1. Every existing daemon test builds ProcessManager through processes.test.ts's `manager()` helper, which always injects `run`; nothing exercised the entry point's wiring. This test boots through `startDaemon` exactly as the entry point does, loads a state with a lingering `done` root past its linger deadline, fires the single `deps.setInterval` callback (index.ts line 923 - the linger sweep, `processManager.expireLinger`), and asserts the removal ran.
fixtureNotes: Reuses the LEGION-104 fixture shape from processes.test.ts (`removes the workspaces of a done root and its done child ...`, ~line 4847): issue `status: "done"`, tree `status: "lingering"`, `<stateDir>/repos/github.com/<owner>/<repo>/.jj` created so `removeIssueWorkspace` runs `jj workspace list`, the workspace directory created so its deletion is observable, a fake runner answering `workspace list` with the workspace name and `log` with commit ids.

The tree carries no `locator`: a finished root whose process already exited (`recordRootExit` clears the locator), so `closeTreeLocked` has nothing to probe or stop and the test isolates the removal leg. `deps.now()` in `daemonTestDependencies` is 2026-08-24T00:00:00Z; `lingerUntil` 2026-08-23 is past.

index.test.ts's `daemonEnvironment.commands.jj` is `/tools/jj`: `createDaemonRunner` (environment.ts 488) rewrites `jj` to that path before the injected runner sees the command, so match `command[0] === "/tools/jj"`. The repo is `acme/widgets`, so the clone is `<stateDir>/repos/github.com/acme/widgets` and the workspace `<stateDir>/workspaces/acme/widgets/widgets-42`.

`console.error` calls are joined whole (`args.map(String).join(" ")`) so the `failed to remove ...` line carries its Error text; the `failed to remove` assertion comes FIRST so the RED run prints the guard's message verbatim (that is the quote the handoff and PR body need).

Boot leaves a lingering tree alone (`reconcileAdmission` demotes only active-no-locator trees; `reconnectRoots` arms deadlines only for active/dead ones), and the linger callback also fires `reconcileOrphans`/`reconcileWorkerAdmission`, which the base runner answers with empty stdout. `flushEventLoopUntil` (already in the file, line 51) waits for `status === "closed"`, which the close reaches on RED too (the failure is logged, the close continues), so the test cannot hang on unfixed code.

code: it("removes a done root's workspace when the linger sweep closes its tree: the entry point hands ProcessManager its command runner (LEGION-163)", async () => {
state.issues[root] = { key: root, title: "Finished root", status: "done", children: [] };
// A finished root past its linger deadline whose process is already gone (`recordRootExit`
// cleared the locator): the sweep's close has nothing to stop, only the workspace to remove.
// `removeIssueWorkspace` asks jj only when the shared clone exists (`<clone>/.jj`).
if (!baseRunner) throw new Error("daemonTestDependencies did not supply a runner");
// Each `console.error` call joined whole, so a `failed to remove ...` line carries its error.
// The daemon runner resolves `jj` to the environment's `/tools/jj` before this fake
// index.ts arms exactly one interval: the linger sweep (`processManager.expireLinger`).
await rm(stateDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
expect(errorLogs.filter((line) => line.includes("failed to remove the workspace of"))).toEqual(
`[legion] removed the workspace of ${root} (${workspaceDir}) at the close of tree ${root}: abandoned 1 commit(s) nothing else reached`
